fot_token_configured.meaning: a fee-on-transfer token is configured as the disputeToken

dispute_amount.meaning: disputeAmount tokens sent by the user to disputeTree()

fot_fee_deducted.meaning: the FoT token deducts a transfer fee on the deposit

legitimate_use.meaning: the scenario occurs through legitimate protocol use rather than a malicious attack

tree_publish_blocked.meaning: no new Merkle trees can be published and tree revocation is blocked

assumptions: The disputeToken is a fee-on-transfer token whose deposit fee is deducted before the contract balance is credited.
The scenario arises from legitimate protocol use, not a malicious attack.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the governor or disputer is the caller of resolveDispute() in the failing transaction, so the caller qualifier of the resolution scenario cannot be bound.
Report does not establish a concrete prior on-chain state (e.g., an actual disputeTree transaction) beyond the conditional scenario, so the tree-publishing precondition state is not bound.

limitations: The selected impact i_tree_updates_blocked is a downstream consequence of resolveDispute() reverting; the plan formalizes only that tree publishing/revocation is blocked, not the revert mechanism itself.
The relation is expressed as a Boolean absence of the blocked-tree outcome because the report gives no numeric definition of tree publication capacity or revocation state.
Other reported impacts (disputer remaining non-zero, frozen claims) are handled in separate claim-generation passes and are not covered by this plan.
